description:
Runtime-demand propagation treats `BinaryOp` and `UnaryOp` as removable when their result is ignored:

- `src/compiler2/jobs/runtime_demand.rs:2285-2289`
- `src/compiler2/jobs/runtime_demand.rs:2291-2295`

In that case operands are not demanded and may receive `Nothing` transport layouts. Backend lowering nevertheless emits both operations unconditionally:

- `src/compiler2/jobs/backend.rs:1896-1901`
- `src/compiler2/jobs/backend.rs:1902-1906`

That lets an emitted operation read an operand the transport plan correctly erased.

## Minimal reproducer

```fz
fn main() do
  t = {1, 2}
  not (t == t)
  dbg(:ok)
end
```

At `a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83`:

- `fz2 interp` fails with `backend value 3 is unbound`.
- `fz2 run` and `fz2 build` panic in native lowering because `v3` is runtime-absent.
- The backend dump shows equality result `v3` and ignored unary result `v4` with `nothing` layouts, while the delivered-resume entry still contains `v4 = Not v3`.

The equality call's ignored return is erased correctly; the surviving `UnaryOp` is the invalid read.

## Strategy

Make symbolic backend lowering honor the existing runtime-absence proof for `BinaryOp` and `UnaryOp`, as it does for other result-producing runtime-pure steps. Prefer a helper name/contract describing omission of any runtime-pure absent-result step rather than extending "fresh construction" terminology.

Update fact-engine/backend documentation so it states which step families are omitted and why: runtime demand already declares that these operators need no operands when their result is ignored.

## Acceptance

- Add the reproducer as an intent-named behavioral fixture.
- It prints `:ok` on `interp`, `run`, and `build`.
- Symbolic backend contains no executable `UnaryOp` reading the absent equality result; it lowers the absent-result operator to `BackendStep::Omitted`.
- Apply and directly test the invariant for both `BinaryOp` and `UnaryOp`. If source normalization does not reliably produce a `BinaryOp`, use focused backend-lowering test construction.
- Existing runtime-demand, backend canonicalization, fixture-matrix, and native bound-before-use tests remain green.
- Update `.agent/docs/fact-engine.md` and backend helper comments to match expanded omission contract.
title: [BUG] Omit runtime-absent BinaryOp/UnaryOp steps before they read erased operands
